record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Suppose (p1,N, ..., pℓ,N) is a good sequence of ℓ-tuples of real polynomials in the sense defined in the paper. Must it follow that for every ergodic system (X, X, μ, T) and bounded measurable functions f1, ..., fℓ, the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{[p1,N(n)]}f1 · ... · T^{[pℓ,N(n)]}fℓ converge in L^2 to (∫ f1 dμ) · ... · (∫ fℓ dμ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 10. Suppose that the sequence of `-tuples of polynomials (p1,N , . . . , p`,N ) is good. Show that for every ergodic system (X, X , µ, T) and functions f1, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ) we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 T^[p1,N (n)]f1 · · · T^[p`,N (n)]f` = ∫ f1 dµ · · · ∫ f` dµ where convergence takes place in L^2(µ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let (X, 𝓧, μ, T) be an invertible measure-preserving system, and for any real number r write [r] for the integer part of r. For each N ≥ 1 let (p_{1,N}, …, p_{ℓ,N}) be an ℓ-tuple of real polynomials in one variable. Call the sequence of ℓ-tuples ((p_{1,N}, …, p_{ℓ,N}))_{N∈ℕ} "good" if for every ergodic invertible measure-preserving system (X, 𝓧, μ, T) and all f_1, …, f_ℓ ∈ L^∞(μ), the limit

   lim_{N→∞} (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^{N} T^{[p_{1,N}(n)]} f_1 · T^{[p_{2,N}(n)]} f_2 ⋯ T^{[p_{ℓ,N}(n)]} f_ℓ

exists in L^2(μ).

Question. Suppose that the sequence of ℓ-tuples (p_{1,N}, …, p_{ℓ,N}), N ∈ ℕ, is good in the sense above. Is it then true that, for every ergodic invertible measure-preserving system (X, 𝓧, μ, T) and all f_1, …, f_ℓ ∈ L^∞(μ),

   lim_{N→∞} (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^{N} T^{[p_{1,N}(n)]} f_1 ⋯ T^{[p_{ℓ,N}(n)]} f_ℓ = (∫ f_1 dμ) ⋯ (∫ f_ℓ dμ)

in L^2(μ)?
artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress on joint ergodicity for polynomial iterates has been made (Frantzikinakis–Kuca and others, 2022–2025), settling many cases including pairwise independent and linearly independent polynomial families, and extending to functions of polynomial growth. However, no source explicitly confirms a complete affirmative answer for arbitrary good sequences of variable polynomial ℓ-tuples; the general question appears to remain open or only partially resolved.

status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions for joint ergodicity; settles several conjectures on multiple ergodic averages with polynomial iterates.
status_evidence.claim: Substantial partial progress on related joint ergodicity questions.

status_evidence.snippet: Joint ergodicity criteria for Hardy field functions of polynomial growth.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress in related settings.
